LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_ONE.titleTraditional: 數字 + 量詞 + 名詞
LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_ONE.learnerPromise: Ask for and say how many people, books, flowers, or gifts there are.
LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_ONE.explanation: Chinese needs a measure word between a number and noun: 個 for general nouns, 本 for books, and 朵 for flowers. Before a measure word, say 兩 for “two,” not 二.

teachingGlossary.meaning: connects a describing word or owner to a thing
how about it; okay or not
what about; asks the question back

LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_ONE.pattern: Number or 幾 + measure word + noun

discoveryLab.title: Pick the right measure word
discoveryLab.description: The measure word links the number to the thing. The thing you name chooses the measure word.

choices.label: Books · 本
choices.note: Use 本 for books and similar things.

choices.label: Flowers · 朵
choices.note: 朵 counts flowers. 幾 still needs a measure word.

choices.label: General · 個
choices.note: 個 is the useful general measure word in this lesson.

choices.label: Repair “two”
choices.pinyin: èr běn shū → liǎng běn shū
choices.note: Use 兩 before a measure word when counting two things.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Put them in order: number + measure word + thing: 兩 + 本 + 書.

items.question: Do I need a word between the number and the thing?
items.answer: Yes — a measure word. Number and thing never sit side by side.

items.question: Why do I say 兩 for "two" here, not 二?
items.answer: Before a measure word, two becomes 兩. 二 is only for plain counting, like 一二三.

items.question: Can I count everything with 個?
items.answer: No. 個 is the general one, but books take 本 and flowers take 朵.

text.traditional: A：你有幾個台灣朋友？ B：我有三個台灣朋友。
text.simplified: A：你有几个台湾朋友？ B：我有三个台湾朋友。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yǒu jǐ ge Táiwān péngyǒu? B: Wǒ yǒu sān ge Táiwān péngyǒu.
text.english: A: How many Taiwanese friends do you have? B: I have three Taiwanese friends.

text.traditional: A：你有幾本中文書？ B：我有五本中文書。
text.simplified: A：你有几本中文书？ B：我有五本中文书。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yǒu jǐ běn Zhōngwén shū? B: Wǒ yǒu wǔ běn Zhōngwén shū.
text.english: A: How many Chinese books do you have? B: I have five Chinese books.

text.traditional: A：你們有幾個新同學？ B：我們有兩個新同學。
text.simplified: A：你们有几个新同学？ B：我们有两个新同学。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐmen yǒu jǐ ge xīn tóngxué? B: Wǒmen yǒu liǎng ge xīn tóngxué.
text.english: A: How many new classmates do you have? B: We have two new classmates.

questions.correctFeedback: 兩 gives the quantity, and 朵 is the measure word for flowers.
questions.repairFeedback: Flowers use 朵. For “two” before a measure word, choose 兩.

tiles.pinyin: wǒ yào mǎi sān ge shū

questions.repairFeedback: Keep the three-part quantity together: 三 + 本 + 書.

tiles.pinyin: nǐ yǒu jǐ běn Yīngwén shū
tiles.meaning: how many English books do you have

LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_TWO.learnerPromise: Say who gives what gift to whom.
LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_TWO.explanation: After 送, say the receiver first and the gift second: 送 + person + gift. Unlike English, Chinese adds no “to” before the receiver.

teachingGlossary.meaning: connects a describing word or owner to a thing
how about it; okay or not
what about; asks the question back

discoveryLab.title: Put the person first, then the gift
discoveryLab.description: 送 takes two things after it: first the person who gets the gift, then the gift itself.

choices.label: Person then gift
choices.pinyin: Māma sòng wǒ yí ge lǐwù.
choices.note: 我 is the receiver. 一個禮物 is the gift.

choices.label: Ask for the person
choices.english: Who will you give cake to?
choices.note: 誰 asks for the person who gets the gift.

choices.label: Ask for the gift
choices.english: What would you like to give Mom?
choices.note: 媽媽 names the person who gets the gift. 什麼 asks for the gift.

choices.label: Repair the order
choices.traditional: 我送一本書她 → 我送她一本書
choices.simplified: 我送一本书她 → 我送她一本书
choices.pinyin: Wǒ sòng yì běn shū tā → wǒ sòng tā yì běn shū
choices.note: Keep the receiver before the gift.

patternRows.english: I would like to give her flowers.
Who will you give cake to?

items.question: Do I say the gift first or the person first after 送?
items.answer: Person first, then the gift. There is no word for "to" in Chinese here.

right.pinyin: Wǒ sòng tā yì běn shū.

items.question: How do I ask WHO gets the gift — 誰 or 什麼?
items.answer: 誰 asks for the person who receives it. 什麼 asks for the gift itself.

right.english: Who will you give the cake to?

items.question: 想 and 要 both mean "want". Do I need both?
items.answer: No, just one. 想 is a soft "would like to"; 要 is a firmer "plan to".

right.pinyin: Wǒ yào mǎi yì běn shū.
right.english: I want to buy a book.

text.traditional: A：你想送媽媽什麼？ B：我想送她花。
text.simplified: A：你想送妈妈什么？ B：我想送她花。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ xiǎng sòng māma shénme? B: Wǒ xiǎng sòng tā huā.
text.english: A: What would you like to give Mom? B: I would like to give her flowers.

text.traditional: A：你要送誰蛋糕？ B：我要送老師蛋糕。
text.simplified: A：你要送谁蛋糕？ B：我要送老师蛋糕。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yào sòng shéi dàngāo? B: Wǒ yào sòng lǎoshī dàngāo.
text.english: A: Who will you give cake to? B: I will give the teacher cake.

text.traditional: A：你想送他什麼禮物？ B：我想送他一本中文書。
text.simplified: A：你想送他什么礼物？ B：我想送他一本中文书。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ xiǎng sòng tā shénme lǐwù? B: Wǒ xiǎng sòng tā yì běn Zhōngwén shū.
text.english: A: What gift would you like to give him? B: I would like to give him a Chinese book.

questions.correctFeedback: 爸爸 is the giver, 他 is the receiver, and 一本書 is the gift.
questions.repairFeedback: Use giver + 送 + person + gift. The picture makes 他 the receiver.

questions.correctFeedback: 想 comes before 送, then the receiver 她 comes before the cake.
